title: Giri Babu, Telugu Cinema's Versatile Face of Five Decades, Dies at 80
excerpt: Born Yerra Seshagiri Rao, the actor moved from hero to villain to beloved character artiste across more than 600 Telugu films, and also produced and directed.
body:
• Veteran Telugu actor Giri Babu, born Yerra Seshagiri Rao, died on Saturday, November 14, at a private hospital in Hyderabad. He was 80.
  • Across nearly five decades he acted in more than 600 Telugu films, moving from hero to villain and comedy roles before becoming a familiar character artiste; he also produced and directed films.
  • Chiranjeevi, Mohan Babu, Nandamuri Balakrishna and Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan led the tributes from the Telugu film industry.
  • His mortal remains were kept at the Film Chamber on Saturday evening for public homage, with final rites scheduled for Sunday, November 15, at his native Ravinuthala, the Movie Artistes Association said.

Giri Babu, one of Telugu cinema's most familiar faces across five decades, died on Saturday at a private hospital in Kondapur, Hyderabad, following a prolonged age-related illness, Telangana Today reported. He was 80. Born Yerra Seshagiri Rao, he was known to generations of Telugu audiences simply as Giri Babu — a performer who could headline a film as its hero, menace it as its villain, and, in his later years, anchor it as a character artiste.

A career that crossed every role

Giri Babu was born on June 8, 1946, in Ravinuthala village of Korisapadu mandal in Prakasam district, and entered films with Jagame Maya. He began as a hero, then built a long second act in villain and comedy roles before settling into the supporting parts for which younger audiences know him best. Over nearly five decades, he acted in more than 600 films, according to The Times of India. His final screen appearance was in the 2023 film Anni Manchi Sakunamule.

He also worked behind the camera. As a producer he made Simha Garjana, Merupudadi and Indrajith, and as a director he made Ranarangam, Indrajith and Nee Sukhame Ne Korukunna.

'We were roommates in Madras'

The tributes that followed spoke less about filmography than about the man. Mohan Babu, who shared a room with Giri Babu in their struggling days in Madras, said in a statement carried by the Deccan Chronicle:

"When we were in Madras, Giribabu and I were roommates. He entered the film industry before me. I am unable to find words to express my grief."

— Mohan Babu, actor

Nandamuri Balakrishna recalled acting with him at the very start of his own career:

"Giribabu was not just a good actor but also a wonderful human being. His absence is irreparable."

— Nandamuri Balakrishna, actor

Chiranjeevi said on social media that the news had left him shocked, that Giri Babu's distinctive performances and unique style would always be remembered, and called the death a huge loss for the industry. Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan remembered him as equally effective as a villain, a hero and a character artiste, noted his fine sense of humour, and his success as a producer and director.

Family and final rites

Giri Babu's wife died in 2016. He is survived by his family, including his sons Bose Babu and Raghu Babu — Raghu Babu is himself a well-known comedian in Telugu cinema. The Movie Artistes Association said his mortal remains would be kept at the Film Chamber from 7 p.m. to 9 p.m. on Saturday for the public to pay homage, with final rites on Sunday, November 15, between 3 p.m. and 4 p.m. at Ravinuthala, near Medarametla.
